title: EVOLVING ROLLOUTS: Harnessing Historical Experience for Web Agent Evolution in Reinforcement Learning
claim: Group-based RL discards zero-variance failed rollouts; ours distills them into an experience repository that feeds in-context guidance back to the agent.
layout: 2 side-by-side panels, top-to-bottom groups, green arrows to repository and update
description: Two side-by-side panels. The left, gray panel is titled 'Vanilla Reinforcement Learning'. It shows a robot agent above two rollout groups drawn as arrows through Search and Crawl steps with coin icons. Group A is two failed rollouts (red X, R=0) marked 'Long Context' and sent to a trash can labeled 'Discarded'. Group B has one success (green check, R=1) and one failure, and feeds only a small 'Parameter Update' network icon. The right, peach panel is titled 'Evolving Rollouts: Web Agent Evolution'. It has the same two groups, but braces and green arrows send Group A's failed rollouts into an 'Evolving Experience Repository' clipboard icon. A curved green 'In-context Guidance' arrow runs from the repository back to the agent, which now has a lightbulb. Group B still goes to a larger 'Parameter Update' icon. The eye goes first to the discarded trash can and then to the green feedback loop.
caption: The framework of EVOLVING ROLLOUTS. Vanilla group-based reinforcement learning updates parameters only from rollout
abstract: Agentic reinforcement learning (RL) for web search is prohibitively expensive due to long context lengths and costly environment interactions, and this inefficiency is further exacerbated by group-based optimization, which discards learning signals from entire rollout groups with zero reward variance. In this work, we propose EVOLVING ROLLOUTS, an RL framework for web-search agents that moves beyond episodic training and distills collected rollouts into in-context guidance for future policy behavior. By extracting the reward-labeled trajectories into strategic experiences, our method augments standard parameter-space optimization with implicit context-space optimization guided by prior experience. This enables the agent to recover learning signals from zero-variance rollouts, thereby fostering co-evolution between the policy and the experience repository. EVOLVING ROLLOUTS improves sample efficiency and task performance across representative web search benchmarks, with Qwen3-8B surpassing the much larger Qwen3-30B-A3B in average performance across GAIA, xBench, and HLE, and Qwen3-4B attaining comparable results on GAIA and HLE.
